gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-tai-tham: Azonix commands the top with wide-mouthed capitals that barely rise above its lowercase, crisp even when shrunk. And Noto Sans Tai Tham follows in sans-serif lowercase that crowds toward the capital line, so a long stretch feels dense but contemporary.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-tai-viet: Noto Sans Tai Viet brings short ascenders, a tall x-height and terminals pulled back from the curve, all in a plain sans frame beneath Azonix. Azonix answers with wire-straight, shading-free display strokes.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-takri: Azonix is built from stems with no hairlines at all, so every stroke carries the same heft as its neighbors. Noto Sans Takri below leaves its small round letters generously unclosed.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-tamil: Azonix draws its lines with zero modulation, wide and blunt, and its capitals sit barely above the lowercase. But Noto Sans Tamil is the strongest part of the pairing, its terminals stopping far from the stem so text looks magnified.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-tamil-sup: Authoritative from the first glance, the heading is built from plain constant-width lines. Azonix does its best work as a commanding, crisp display voice, while Noto Sans Tamil Supplement handles the quieter job with round forms like open parentheses and a middle band so tall the line looks stocky.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-tangsa: Approachable is the first impression from Noto Sans Tangsa, with wide, inviting round letters and short ascender stems. Azonix, in one unvarying stroke weight, stands next to it like a stern sign beside a friendly face.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-tc: Azonix is drawn like rounded rod, one weight throughout. Noto Sans TC sits beneath it with large open counters and curves that flare outward, so the heavy heading and the easygoing text trade places smoothly.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-telugu: Noto Sans Telugu reads with a high-set midline and counters that stay connected to the outside, giving it a brisk, businesslike manner. Azonix hangs over it like rope, each stem, bowl and tail identical, a firmer partner.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-thaana: Noto Sans Thaana reads friendly, with big open lowercase forms and wide channels into each counter. Over many lines it stays welcoming, while Azonix above it draws every stroke at one thickness.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-thai: Noto Sans Thai reads soft and friendly, its lowercase swollen like inflated glass beads. Azonix is the commanding one, with strokes as thick as drawn wire, while the body font simply leaves its rounded letters open and inviting.
